Our engineering team in Osaka has been using a local AI assistant (running on edge hardware with a 4K token context window) to help navigate our dense Japanese manufacturing documentation. The AI has been silently dropping context mid-conversation, causing confusing and incomplete answers — a serious problem on the factory floor.

We've already installed the context-compaction plugin and the relevant extension files are in place under `.openclaw/extensions/`. However, the current configuration in `.openclaw/openclaw.json` is wrong: the plugin is disabled, the token limits don't match our 4K model, and there's no visibility into what the plugin is doing internally.

Please update `.openclaw/openclaw.json` so that:
1. The context-compaction plugin is properly enabled and tuned for our small 4K-context Japanese-language model.
2. Full debug observability is turned on so our infrastructure team can monitor what the plugin is doing.
3. A dedicated summarization model is explicitly specified (you may use the same model already configured for the session: `mlx-community/japanese-stablelm-base-4k`).

Note that most of our content is Japanese technical text, which has different tokenization characteristics than standard English. The configuration must account for this correctly.
